Area Forecast Discussion...UPDATED
National Weather Service Los Angeles/Oxnard CA 
944 AM PST Fri Nov 20 2026

UPDATED AVIATION SECTION

.SYNOPSIS...19/1001 PM.

Dry weather is expected through at least Sunday afternoon. Highs 
are will be around 5 degrees below normal. Overnight lows will be
chilly as well, with some areas dropping below freezing. Light 
rain is possible Sunday night into Monday and again next 
Wednesday.

&&

.SHORT TERM (TDY-SUN)...20/809 AM.

***UPDATE***

Latest satellite and surface observations indicate clear to partly
cloudy skies across the area (with the partly cloudy conditions
across the Central Coast). On radar, some isolated light showers
are moving south, just off the Central Coast. As for winds,
currently some northerly winds, gusting 25-35 MPH, in the usual
north wind-prone areas.

Forecast-wise for the immediate short term, no significant issues
are expected. Through the day, there will be the possibility of
showers impacting the Central Coast. However, any showers will be
widely scattered and light with no expectation of any issues.
Otherwise, the northerly winds will continue through the day, but
with some weakening this afternoon. High temperatures today will
remain quite cool, only topping out in the mid 50s to mid 60s.

Overall, current forecast has good handle on the immediate short
term. So, no significant updates are expected. 

***From Previous Discussion***

Very benign weather on tap for the next two days in the wake of
ydy's strong storm. Today will start off on the cold side with
many interior areas near or at freezing. Vly dwellers will wake up
to temps in the upper 30s to mid 40s. The only fly in the 
ointment today is a slight chc of a shower this morning across the
Central Coast in the strong northerly flow. Despite ample 
sunshine max temps today will only reach the lower to mid 60s.

Look for another chilly night tonight followed by a sunny and cool
Saturday. Despite all the sunshine and rising hgts from a pop up
ridge max temps will not change much - maybe a 1 to 2 degrees
warmer but still 8-10 degrees blo normal.

A very weak system will move into the area Sunday night into
Monday morning. Rain is likely (70 percent chc) for the Central
Coast, but only a 30 to 40 percent chc south of Pt Concpetion.
Rainfall amounts will be at most a quarter inch of rain along the
Central Coast and a tenth or less to the south.

.LONG TERM (MON-THU)...20/229 AM.

A little stronger ridge will move into the area Monday and will
raise hgts to about 578 dam. This, clear skies and weak offshore
flow will all combine to bring sunny skies and highs in the mid to
upper 60s.

The ridge will not stick around and will be moving to the east on
Tuesday. An approaching upper low will bring increasing clouds
through the day esp to SLO and western SBA counties. Another
degree or two of warming will allow a few sites to reach 70 or 71
degrees.

Another system will move into the area Tuesday night into
Wednesday. While there are still some ensemble members showing a
quarter to a half inch of rain the majority show an event for the
Central Coast with maybe a quarter inch of rain for the Central
Coast (Rocky Butte excepted, of course) and a low chc of a tenth
of an inch south of Pt Conception. Max temps will remain in the
mid 60s to lower 70s.

Thanksgiving should be dry with some offshore flow that will bring
3 to 6 degrees of warming. Most cst/vly locations will see max
temps in the lower to mid 70s or 1 or 2 degrees over normal.

&&

.AVIATION...20/1744Z.

At 1712Z at KLAX, there was no marine layer nor an inversion.

Overall, moderate to high confidence in 18Z TAF Package.
Timing of LIFR conditions may be off +/- 2 hours at KPRB.
15% chance of LIFR conditions at KSMX 21/12-16Z.

KLAX...High confidence in VFR TAF. Westerly winds will shift
to the NW-N around 10 kts this evening. Weakening and turning
easterly after midnight with good confidence that east wind
component remains below 7 kts.

KBUR...High confidence in VFR TAF.

&&

.MARINE...20/803 AM.

Conditions across the coastal waters have significantly improved
from yesterday. However, conditions will remain hazardous to
small craft through tonight becoming relatively mild by Saturday.
A weak front will move across the coastal waters Sunday into 
Monday but minimal impacts are expected at this time. 

A stronger cold front is likely to impact the coastal waters
Tuesday night into Wednesday. Best chances for wind and rain
are likely to be off the Central coast due the front weakening 
on approach. Post-frontal low-end SCA level NW-W winds will 
still be possible Wednesday/night south of Point Conception. 
Large seas are also expected to return to the coastal waters 
around mid to late next week.

&&

.BEACHES...20/811 AM.

Elevated to high surf will create dangerous rip currents and 
beach conditions today. High Surf Advisories remain in effect for 
the Central Coast and Ventura Coast through 11 AM this morning, 
but even after that time strong rip currents are likely along most
westerly facing beaches. As swell height subsides, surf will 
gradually subside with relatively small surf for most beaches by 
Saturday. 

Extremely high tides, likely record breaking, will occur over
Thanksgiving week (peaking Tuesday through Thanksgiving Day). 
Additional large westerly swells are becoming increasingly likely
during the coming week as well. These swells have a good chance 
of producing a period of high surf for west facing beaches.

The combination of very high tides and increasing surf next week 
will likely lead to at least moderate-level, widespread coastal 
flooding issues across all coasts. There is potential for 
significant coastal flooding impacts if a larger swell overlaps 
with the timing of the extreme tides - that would likely occur
Wednesday and Thursday.
